title: Josslyn Jacks Reveals the 1 Reason She Can't Get Over Her Sonny Hate
metaDescription: Does Josslyn need to get over her Sonny hate on General Hospital? Fans are split as her grudge against Sonny Corinthos drags on. Vote now.
author: Mia Carter
html:
Josslyn Jacks has made one thing clear on General Hospital: she is not ready to forgive Sonny Corinthos. The daughter of Carly Spencer and Jasper Jacks has spent years watching Sonny's choices tear through her family, and she has decided she will not pretend otherwise. That stubbornness has split the fandom right down the middle.

The question now is simple. Does Josslyn need to get over her Sonny hate, or is she right to hold the line? Fans cannot agree, and the debate has become one of the loudest arguments in the soap community.

Why Josslyn's Sonny Hate Runs So Deep

Josslyn did not wake up one morning and decide to despise her stepfather. Her resentment grew out of real history. Sonny has been a permanent fixture in her mother's life for years, and that connection has brought violence, secrets, and grief into the family more than once.

She watched Carly get pulled back into Sonny's orbit again and again. She watched the mob world follow him home. For Josslyn, the cost of loving Sonny has always been paid by the people around him, not by Sonny himself.

That is the core of her position. She is not angry about one bad night or one broken promise. She is angry about a pattern, and she has decided she is done excusing it.

Does Josslyn Need to Get Over Her Sonny Hate?

That is the exact question fans are arguing about right now. One side says Josslyn is holding a grudge that no longer serves her. They point out that Sonny is family, that Carly has made her own choices, and that Josslyn's refusal to bend only keeps her trapped in the past.

The other side says she owes him nothing. Sonny has hurt her mother, her brother, and her extended family. Forgiveness is not a requirement, and nobody gets to demand it on a timeline that suits them.

Both arguments have weight. The real tension is that Josslyn's Sonny hate has become part of her identity, and letting it go would mean admitting something complicated about the people she loves most.

What Fans Are Saying About the Grudge

Soap viewers rarely agree on anything, and this fight is no exception. Some fans call Josslyn immature for refusing to move on. They argue that Sonny has protected Carly and the kids more times than anyone counts, and that Josslyn only sees the damage.

Others say she is the only person in Port Charles telling the truth. They see her as the one character who refuses to pretend the mob life is normal, and they respect her for it.

Either way, the argument keeps General Hospital fans talking, and that is exactly what a good soap rivalry is supposed to do.

The Bigger Picture for Josslyn and Sonny

Josslyn is no longer a kid watching from the sidelines. She is a young woman making her own choices, and her feelings about Sonny reflect that shift. She gets to decide who she trusts.

Sonny, for his part, has never been great at accepting rejection. He tends to expect loyalty, and Josslyn's cold shoulder cuts against everything he believes about family.

That friction is what makes the story work. It is not just a feud. It is a clash between two people who both think they are protecting the same woman.

So does Josslyn need to get over her Sonny hate? Maybe not today. Maybe not ever. But the question itself is what keeps the drama alive, and fans will keep picking sides as long as the writers keep the fire burning.

Where do you land? Is Josslyn right to hold the grudge, or is it time she let it go?
